## Design

### 2026-10-12 – October 12

**14h**

October 12

Fortunately today I didn't have school so i spent my entire day working on this project, though I do have experience with CAD before with robotics, I never worked on building a product, and they each have their differences is one thing I've realized.

So I first designed the base with the necessary holes for the usb cable, along with walls and mounting bosses
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/63fea2556350619e7ce42c693bf137f331c73368acacfc991cfb6f167ebde8e4.png)

Then I had to design the top plate, individual with 61 keys, all sketched to be precise and in the exact correct locations
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/81488abb9d418eda456a8d6d5eb24d13ef1609cfc01ca66437814db74f4e6cab.png)

Then I created a simple knob, that didn't take too long,
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/b6ff037bdfd8d0861df665ab1d0a041f7498a32e9f3304bf9561841da5a4187a.png)

After this I assembled everything, and this is when I found out I could export the KiCad PCB onto fusion
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/94c5d783fd7a137563b83ae3ec7f736276dfa7743639bc4880b52d659a6b8b6f.png)

I put the PCB intot eh Case, and matched the position with the 4 mounting bosses, I positioned the PCB underside at 21mm above the case floor origin, with the plate hidden to inspect the placement
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/b695834b8e2c2ad00f89bf91b506d5b478b14a9c57436604c357e01d5dfd0215.png)

For simulation purposes to make sure the holes were in the right spot, I put on the back side to see that there wasn't any interference, and I checked the important Pico against the USB pocket and BOOTSEL opening. This was purely a visual inspection to take notes, however plug insertion and cable bending will remain untested as of now.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/4cdccad16b5756471d26790eba4cbbf5a4fd2d5ffec95c21dd051b405db2d48d.png)

After that I had to restore the switch plate, and I placed that above the PCB to inspect the key opening alignment. But the switch and Keycap models are not in this KiCad export, something I might have to work on tomorrow to make it a clean and finished product.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/a9eb3ecc58854c00c2e495198fa05b668f2e0ad9765372f6ec1a9ffeaac81a48.png)

From here I added 4 spacer solids at the mounting hole positions, starting at the planned PCB top height of 22.6mm. They provide the 3.5mm plate gap,
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/3d77d970f468aa33ce74176e85b14b46469a0fc791905f576bba3b8e9c1bd479.png)

And this is where I got to the point where majority of the cad was completed but of course, I didn't want it to look as simple as this, so I went back to planning some other features to make it look more stylish similar to ones on the internet.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/ae3bfc629d555a3d9642b1174c2ef9cad7a4d1b88fe4050e389d0c1d6c74c934.png)

But before I wanted to do so, I just wanted to check how expensive printing would take. So I uploaded my not finished file to see shipping charges and estimated cost.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/c1716fd71576f8b2e4f646fed807b247fbfc6ac6394a3f640712503f7de4f4cf.png)

Unfortunate the service rejected the full width parts and tiny spacers, so I checked resin and combining the spacers
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/5510dfc2087421e662f84f0162ec67af8eb60f37343d540a54b12723b5175346.png)

To continue from my original plans I needed to design a v2, but I wanted to finish a v1 to show change in design strategy so I continued working on v1 which I hopefully would never use, but worst case scenario if I didn't have time to finish v2. so I first found measurements online and matched them with my PCB for  a 1U keycap.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/c2f37565a3caf6835ab1cdc8446b6142063ac60a9cc44d7106025865d02adc8c.png)

Then the 6.25U ANSI spacebar, also measured exactly.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/ba60f3e95576955dbd571d7d48bb38f88f077d97d0646d29ec53d7e54e5b8c78.png)

For the spacebar I had to do an extra step as part of the underside, because on my PCB the sensor button was in the center, so the clicking feature had to be there as well, the left and right side weights were added to make it feel heavier and more balanced, a common technique keyboard builders use (source: instagram reels).
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/2e6154245066f3390249da4515d945793fd5259e812f895f09a568a8680c4c75.png)

I also created the other keys that I would need according to the specifications and I completed the assembly for v1.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/0f34e2abc7fff960a3dc12d7100985c85658bfe0980233a1dd89035ba91c0792.png)

I few changes following this for v2, would be adding a screen underneath the volume cylinder, and making the keyboard thinner to look better, and possibly color customization. The total time of 14 hours was the amount of time I did work, of course I took breaks in between, and those aren't calculated for this entry

### 2026-10-14 – October 13

**10h**

October 13

Now that I completed v1, I wanted to adjust it to work on v2, so I got the switch model. This was a substitute switch that I found online for the Gateron switch in my cart.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/a9439fdff3914cb030ba8166e58f6b046524618f8fcc0a234f7b174503c9a2c7.png)

Next to make the design more sleek I reduced the case height from 27.6mm to 17.1mm. The shell thickness was changed to 2mm for the floor and lower walls
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/748bac7a58015556aded41f3bee49c16c5cc6aea67a79f76991abcf6056daaee.png)

I added the PCB mounting bosses in the hole coordinates, and positioned 10.5 mm above the origin. Unfortunately the newer slim version now needs the Pico headers soldered instead of tall sockets.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/6fc2f4d22d5f6451fd58f4ed28b6584c6518119627eec316fff1a33fb9e90433.png)

I had to redo the controller access openings again for the underside USB pocket, cable channel, BOOTSEL and reset opening to a thinner base, this time I did it much faster knowing the exact position to put it in and size
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/61ed20efff7332f23960d8274ce49d6575b419c968c411417b086c28c4815cfd.png)

I also had to redo the upper plate because the dimensions of the PCB changed, I wish I could've kept it the same but it was faster this time, but still as tedious as picking every hole.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/a8796b016603d5ca15d477bbfaf55e50556c54a395244eef32f7372ff39ff278.png)

For the knob mount this time I looked at the Adafruit encoder specs to make sure the hole is perfect enough to fit it and I also added underside support walls. Finding the specs was difficult as it wasn't on the website so I searched on Reddit and I found the necessary dimensions.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/3742783eb9425d21b220aa0f3443eb273e142ea33063e8334121b80131d3664d.png)

I added a goal which was to have a tall portrait display to show volume. The bottom margin is 17.2mm and the gap to the knob is 13.6mm. The TFT body is a dimensional envelope.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/c607fdf668c1dc84130b19d7ec99b6e1117bff5c8019557041a0958f4b9c47c3.png)

Then after that I had a long tedious process of putting all the generic MX models and adding all 61 keys and joined them with he joint tool on fusion. This was arguably the longest process on this entire job, but the image you see has the case hidden.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/ee11487df47d472ed82b476d9d6044b7a40e61101ad82f89599d6307458b796c.png)

I also manually engraved all 61 keycaps to have the letter, this way its not tedious to put all the stickers. The engravings were 0.35mm deep into the keycap. These are just reference ones for now.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/191843e8f40d8651724bfc78287df1e988df4c0d99d20d5f033446ad7bacb02f.png)

Then I made the full assembly for this project so far the design is much better than earlier somewhat but there are some final tweaks that could be made
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/46e822e54e33134beb902170a353a79f668169c356e1f3036b478680dcd73a51.png)

### 2026-10-15 – October 15

**2h**

October 15

Today I decided to do research on the display to see dimensions, mounting hole pitch, active area and header placement with this i corrected the hole in my PCB cuz it was an estimate earlier, but the small pin to floor margins still need physical verification.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/ae207408085129bc7770f0de35db4efbc72979116b35c172856672cd5ad52355.png)

Next I did the MX Socket geometry, cross sockets were added tot he keycap bottoms including the multiple stabilizer positions.  Print the fit gauge and test actual switches before printing the full set.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/41f18e09b1992552c4d2eb7cadd05e95bf2ed84d42e9181137aa47cfdbfcf37b.png)
